content:
We need to find a retrosynthetic template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the described carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id.

We have tools: search_template_catalog_by_criteria, get_template, apply_template, etc.

We need to search for templates that match forward reaction: break C=O and C=C, form C-O and C-C, produce five-membered ring, aliphatic hydroxyl, etc.

We have the target molecule (product) given as SMILES with atom mapping numbers. That is the product of the forward reaction? Actually the description: "In a carbonyl-ene reaction, an alkene reacts with an allylic hydrogen and a carbonyl group to form a new carbon-carbon bond... The result is formation of new C-C bond and new stereocenter... one substituent is hydroxyl." So forward reaction: starting material has alkene and carbonyl; product has hydroxyl and new C-C bond, forming a five-membered ring.

We have the product SMILES (with mapping). We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse) to this product gives precursors (alkene + carbonyl). The template ID is the one used to search the database (not hash). We need to return mapped_rxn (presumably the reaction SMILES with atom mapping) associated with that template.

Thus steps: search template catalog with criteria: bonds broken: C=O, C=C; bonds formed: C-C, C-O; functional groups broken: "ketones", "C-C double bonds"; functional groups formed: "aliphatic hydroxyl", "five-membered rings". Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria.

Let's call that.
